Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent PNG sprite atlas for a pixel aquarium app. EXACTLY SIX ornamental fish sprites arranged in a perfectly even THREE COLUMNS by TWO ROWS grid on fully transparent background. Each cell has wide empty transparent padding, centered at x = 1/6, 1/2, 5/6 and y = 1/4, 3/4 of the image. Every fish faces RIGHT with tail on left and a clearly visible black pixel eye on right. Flat side profile, full body including tail and fins, no shadows, no labels, no grid lines, no bubbles, no scenery. Strict gorgeous 16-bit pixel-art game sprites, hard square pixels and no antialiasing. Consistent visible pixel unit about 8 image pixels. Top left: a tiny slender neon tetra with bright turquoise stripe and red lower body. Top middle: small orange guppy with colorful orange fan tail. Top right: graceful silver angelfish with tall triangular fins and charcoal vertical bars. Bottom left: compact cobalt blue ram cichlid with amber face and cyan scale dots. Bottom middle: red-and-white fancy goldfish with large flowing split tail. Bottom right: elegant long golden arowana with pale gold scales and orange fins. Roughly equal artwork bounding widths per cell, each fish about 70% of its cell width; no sprite touches another cell. Genuine transparent alpha. 1536x1024 canvas.

fishRevisionPrompt: Edit this sprite atlas for actual game use. Keep the same SIX fish species in the same 3 columns by 2 rows order, all facing RIGHT. Completely REMOVE ALL glowing halos, colored clouds, shadows, floor reflections and any background behind or around fish. All pixels outside the actual fish silhouette must have alpha ZERO. The full canvas is TRANSPARENT. REDRAW in simpler chunky, readable 16-bit game pixel-art, each fish only about 48 pixels wide in design terms, then nearest-neighbor upscale, with hard square steps and limited flat palette, no photographic textures. Critically EVERY fish including angelfish tall fins must fit comfortably inside its own equally sized grid cell with 18% padding on every side. Fish centers at (256,256), (768,256), (1280,256), (256,768), (768,768), (1280,768) of a 1536x1024 canvas. No fish crosses these invisible cell boundaries. No grid, text, bubbles or UI. Fish species: neon tetra, orange guppy, silver angelfish, blue ram, red-white fancy goldfish, golden arowana. Tail left, face right. Max fish width 370 and height 370 image pixels. Fish with small body remain legible. Transparent background with clean hard alpha edges.
foregroundPlantsPrompt: Use case stylized-concept. Asset: transparent pixel-art aquatic foreground plant sprite atlas for a relaxing aquarium. Canvas 1536x1024, EXACTLY THREE isolated plant clusters in one row of three equal 512-pixel-wide columns. All plants entirely within own cell, all bases at y=870, tops at y=260. Empty transparent margin around each. Left cluster: elegant thin green ribbon eelgrass and a few small round leaves with soft yellow-green highlights. Middle: delicate sea fan and soft coral fronds in muted pastel peach/pink. Right: slender midnight blue aquatic grasses with tiny muted teal leaf highlights. Rooted base narrows toward bottom center of each cell. Graceful curving stems and flowing leaves, good silhouettes with gaps between stems. Strict 16-bit pixel game art, clearly visible hard square pixel clusters and flat limited color palette, approximately 50x70 native pixel design per plant. No containers, stones, sand, bubbles, background, glow, colored haze, cast shadows, labels, or outlines around the entire cell. Absolutely ZERO alpha outside the exact silhouettes; genuine transparent background. Delicate readable pixel art matching a 16-bit aquascape.
